# Vendored circuit fixtures

Generated files, copied from the circuits repository at
`~/Code/mirage/circuits`. Do not edit them by hand: they are the authority the
Solidity encoder and verifier are checked against, and a hand-edit makes a
passing test meaningless.

| File | Source | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `statement.json` | `test/vectors/statement.json` | `test/StatementHash.t.sol` |
| `commitment.json` | `test/vectors/commitment.json` | reference, spec 8.3 |
| `proof.json` | `contracts/proof.json` | `test/EscrowZK.t.sol` |

They live here because Foundry cannot read outside its project root, so the
tests cannot reach the circuits repo directly.

## Regenerating

From the circuits repository:

```sh
cargo run -p mirage-encoding --bin gen-vectors
cargo run -p mirage-prover --release --bin export-verifier
```

Then copy the three files back:

```sh
cp test/vectors/statement.json test/vectors/commitment.json \
   ../escrow/test/fixtures/
cp contracts/proof.json ../escrow/test/fixtures/
cp contracts/Verifier.sol ../escrow/src/Verifier.sol
```

`Verifier.sol` is regenerated by the same command and belongs in `src/`, not
here: it is compiled rather than read.

## When these must be regenerated

- The spec 8.3 or 10.2 encoding changes. Both the circuit and
  `src/StatementHash.sol` must change with it, and a mismatch surfaces only as
  "proof rejected".
- The relation changes, which produces a new verifying key. `Verifier.sol` and
  `proof.json` must be regenerated together; an old proof will not verify
  against a new key.
- The fixture's statement context changes, for example its payout asset. The
  escrow test reconstructs that context from `proof.json`, so the two travel
  together.
